textbookText: Section 'B'
Very short answer type questions.
1. Write any one condition at which a body of certain mass become weightless.
Ans:- A body of certain mass becomes weightless when it is in a state of free fall under the influence of gravity.
2. Name the scientist who propounded the value of gravitational constant.
Ans:- The scientist who propounded the value of the gravitational constant (G) was Sir Henry Cavendish.
3. Write the main conclusion of Galileo's "feather and coin experiment.
Ans:- Galileo concluded that all bodies, regardless of their masses, fall with the same acceleration in the absence of air
resistance.
4. State Newton's universal law of gravitation.

Ans:- Every object in the universe attracts every other object with a force that is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers. Formula:𝐹 = 𝐺 𝑟2 𝑚1𝑚2 5.In which condition will acceleration due to gravity of falling parachute be zero?
Ans:- The acceleration due to gravity of a falling parachute becomes zero when the upward air resistance becomes equal to
the downward gravitational force (i.e., when terminal velocity is reached).
6. Write one effect seen on ocean or sea due to gravitation of the moon and the sun.
Ans:- The gravitation of the moon and the sun causes tides — the periodic rise and fall of sea levels.
7. What are the two factors that affect the force of gravitation?
Ans:- The two factors that affect the force of gravitation are
i) The masses of the two bodies.
ii) The distance between the centers of the two bodies.
8. Define universal gravitational constant G.

Ans:- The universal gravitational constant (G) is the proportionality constant in Newton’s law of gravitation. It is defined as the force of attraction between two bodies of unit masses placed one meter apart in vacuum. Value: G= 6.67 × 𝑁𝑚2/𝑘𝑔2.
9. What is an acceleration due to gravity?
Ans:- Acceleration due to gravity is the acceleration produced in a freely falling body due to the gravitational attraction of
the Earth. It is denoted by g and its average value is 9.8 m/s².
10. What is free fall?
Ans:- Free fall is the motion of a body under the influence of the gravitational force of the Earth only, without any air
resistance. 11. Clarify the statement, "acceleration due to gravity of the earth is 9.8m/s2
Ans:- It means that the velocity of a freely falling object increases by 9.8 meters per second in every second during its fall
toward the Earth.

12. Write the maximum and minimum value of acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the earth. Ans:- 9.83m/s2 is the maximum (at the poles) and 9.78m/s2 is the minimum (at the equator) value of acceleration due to
gravity on earth surface.
13. Write the nature of gravitational force.
Ans:- The gravitational force is always attractive in nature and acts along the line joining the centers of two bodies.
14. Under what conditions is the value of gravitational force equal to the gravitational constant (F=G)?
Ans:- The gravitational force becomes equal to the gravitational constant when the two bodies each have a mass of 1 kg and
are 1 meter apart in vacuum. 15. The acceleration due to gravity of an object of mass 1kg in outer space is 2m/s2.What is the acceleration due to gravity of
another object of the mass 10 kg at the same point? Justify with arguments.
Ans:- The acceleration due to gravity will also be 2 m/s² for the 10 kg object.
Justification: Acceleration due to gravity is independent of the mass of the object; it depends only on the mass and distance of
the planet or celestial body producing the gravity.
Section 'C'
Short answer type questions:
1. When a man travels from Hilly region to Terai region, what will happen to his weight? Explain with reasons.
Ans:- His weight increases because the acceleration due to gravity is greater at lower altitudes (closer to the center of the
Earth).
2. Mass of a body is constant but weight varies from place to place. Why?
Ans:- Mass of a body is constant but weight varies from place to place because weight depends on the acceleration due to
gravity, which changes with altitude and latitude, while mass remains constant everywhere.
3. Acceleration due to gravity of an object 9.8 m/s2. Write two pieces of information that can be obtained from this
statement.
Ans:- Two pieces of information that can be obtained from given statement are
i) The body gains a velocity of 9.8 m/s every second when falling freely.
ii) The object is under the influence of Earth's gravity.
4. By how many times the weight of a body is less on the surface of moon than on the surface of the earth? Why?
Ans:- The weight of a body on the Moon is 1/6th of its weight on Earth because the Moon’s gravitational pull is six times
weaker than Earth’s.
